text.p: Tennis-Big-serving Ivansevic crushes Pescariu
LONDON - Second seed Goran Ivanisevic sounded a warning to his Wimbledon rivals with a ruthless exhibition of power serving on Monday to charge into the second round.

On a gloomy opening day to the championships, thunder reverberated around court two -- both from the skies and the Croat's racket -- as Ivanisevic took just 64 minutes to brush past Romania's Dinu Pescariu 6-1 6-3 6-3.
Tennis-Former champions help launch new show-court

LONDON - Wimbledon's greatest champions did their best to steal local favourite Tim Henman's limelight on Monday as showers delayed the first competitive action on the All England Club's new Number One court.
The official opening of the new show court went ahead as scheduled under threatening skies, with several of tennis's most famous names adding some glamour to the occasion.
Tennis-Rain makes early first appearance at Wimbledon
LONDON - Rain made its first appearance at the Wimbledon tennis championships on Monday, within an hour of the start of the opening day.
Defending champion Richard Krajicek and his opponent Marcello Craca had only just walked out on to Centre Court when the rain began, sending them back to the changing rooms.
Cricket-England openers prosper
LONDON - Openers Michael Atherton and Mark Butcher guided England from the possibility of defeat to the probability of a draw on the final day of the second test at Lord's on Monday.
The pair shared an opening partnership of 162, before Atherton trod on his off-stump playing back to Michael Kasprowicz after scoring 77.
Soccer-Nantes defender Pignol joins French champions Monaco
MONACO - Defender Christophe Pignol signed a three-year contract with French league champions Monaco on Monday in a move from fellow first division Nantes, the club said.
Pignol, 27, was a regular first-choice player for Nantes and is expected to take over the slot vacated at Monaco by Emmanuel Petit, who joined English premier league Arsenal last week.
Soccer-Japan keep alive Asian bid for youth title
KUALA LUMPUR - Japan kept alive Asia's dwindling challenge at the world youth soccer championship when they drew 3-3 with Paraguay on Monday to reach the knockout stage.
Japan, who finished runners-up in group D, now face a second-round clash with Australia, who beat defending champions Argentina 4-2 after Kosta Salapasidis scored all the goals.
Rugby union-Injuries delay Springbok team selection
DURBAN - Springbok centre Edrich Lubbe will miss the rest of the series against the British Lions as South African face a number of injury worries, team officials said on Monday.
Coach Carel du Plessis has had to delay naming his side for Saturday's second test in Durban until Wednesday because of doubts over several players.
Boxing-Italian stripped of gold in scoring row

ROME - Boxing controversy hit the Mediterranean Games on Monday when an Italian heavyweight was stripped of a gold medal in favour of an Algerian after a committee ruled that electronic scoring was faulty.
It was believed to be the first time that the high-tech computerised scoring method used at Olympics and world championships had been overruled.
Athletics-Sestriere meeting at risk
SESTRIERE, Italy - The IAAF international athletics meeting in Sestriere next month could be cancelled if major sponsors do not come forward, organisers said on Monday.
"We are looking for sponsors to cover the costs of this meeting," Livio Berruti, press officer for the company which manages the resort, said.
